title: Kobalos_Malware_Investigation_d37
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential Kobalos malware infection on a high-performance computing (HPC) cluster. Kobalos is a complex malware that targets HPC clusters and other high-profile systems, providing remote access, terminal sessions, and credential stealing capabilities. Your goal is to identify and mitigate the threat.
outcomes: Investigate lateral movement and data exfiltration.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential Kobalos malware infection on a high-performance computing (HPC) cluster. Kobalos is a complex malware that targets HPC clusters and other high-profile systems, providing remote access, terminal sessions, and credential stealing capabilities. Your goal is to identify and mitigate the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the target host, you notice unusual network activity. Investigate the running services on the target host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services.
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, you can use the `netstat` or `ss` command to list all running services and their associated ports. Look for any services that seem out of place or are not part of the standard system services. The suspicious service in this case is running on port 7070.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the list of running services and look for any that seem out of place.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Consider using network monitoring tools to identify unusual ports or services.

levels.title: Lateral Movement Investigation
levels.content: You suspect that the malware might be moving laterally within the network. Investigate the target host to find evidence of file transfers or remote execution used to move between hosts.
levels.solution: To investigate lateral movement, you can check the system logs and network connections for any unusual activity. Look for any evidence of file transfers or remote execution. The service responsible for lateral movement in this case is `payload-transfer.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the system logs and network connections for any unusual activity.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for any evidence of file transfers or remote execution.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: Determine which network port is used for the suspicious communication between the target host and the external command-and-control server.
levels.solution: To determine the network port used for C2 communication, you can analyze the network traffic and identify the port used for the suspicious communication. The port used for C2 communication in this case is 7070.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Analyze the network traffic and identify the port used for the suspicious communication.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Consider using network monitoring tools to identify unusual ports or services.
